description: A fixed 100-concept roadmap for the existing Physics Playground. Never create concept 101.
selection_rule: Fix existing bugs first. Only when the baseline is healthy and no known actionable bug remains may the agent implement the lowest-numbered eligible unfinished concept.

concepts.title: Position, displacement, and reference frames
learning_objectives: Understand position as a vector relative to a chosen coordinate origin.
Calculate vector displacement (Δr = r_f - r_i) independently of the origin.
Transform positions and displacements between different reference frames (translation and rotation).
key_equations: Δr = r_f - r_i = (x_f - x_i, y_f - y_i)
visualization_requirements: 2D cartesian coordinate system with grid and axes
Object moving along a trajectory (circle, linear, oscillation)
Visual vectors for position r_A, displacement Δr, and reference frame B origin O_B and rotated axes
Readouts for coordinates in both global and local reference frames
controls: Reference frame B origin X and Y coordinates
validation_cases: Displacement is invariant under coordinate translation (origin shift)
Rotation transformation correctly rotates coordinates by -θ
Initial and final position difference yields exact displacement vector
concepts.notes: Fully implemented with interactive canvas, coordinate transformation math, readouts, charts, and test coverage.

concepts.title: Distance versus displacement
learning_objectives: Calculate distance as the total path length.
Calculate displacement as the straight-line change in position.
Observe how distance is always greater than or equal to the magnitude of displacement.
visualization_requirements: Trace of the path taken (total distance)
Straight line arrow for displacement vector
Animated object moving along various path types
Real-time counters for distance and displacement magnitude
validation_cases: Displacement is 0 if the path is a closed loop
Distance equals displacement magnitude for unidirectional linear motion
concepts.notes: Implementing with interactive path tracing and real-time scalar vs vector comparison.

concepts.title: Speed and velocity
learning_objectives: Distinguish between average speed (scalar) and average velocity (vector).
Calculate average velocity as displacement divided by time (v_avg = Δr / Δt).
Calculate average speed as total distance divided by time (s_avg = d / Δt).
Observe instantaneous velocity as the rate of change of position.
visualization_requirements: Animated object moving along multiple trajectory types (Linear, Circular, Sine)
Velocity vector arrow (instantaneous velocity) showing direction and magnitude
Real-time readouts for instantaneous speed, velocity vector, and averages
Telemetry graphs for speed and velocity components over time
validation_cases: Average velocity is zero for any closed-loop path completed in time T
Average speed equals magnitude of constant velocity for unidirectional linear motion
Instantaneous speed is always the magnitude of the instantaneous velocity vector
concepts.notes: Implementing interactive speed vs velocity comparison with vector visualization.

concepts.title: Acceleration
learning_objectives: Understand acceleration as the rate of change of velocity (vector and scalar).
Distinguish between constant linear acceleration, free-fall acceleration, and centripetal acceleration.
Observe kinematic relationships: v = v_0 + at and x = x_0 + v_0 t + 1/2 a t^2.
Visualize acceleration vector arrows alongside velocity and position.
visualization_requirements: Animated object moving along trajectory (Linear Accelerated, Free Fall, Circular Motion)
Velocity vector (green) and Acceleration vector (rose/red) arrows
Real-time telemetry and numerical readouts for position, velocity, and acceleration
Physics charts plotting velocity and acceleration components over time
controls: Motion mode (Linear Acceleration, Free Fall, Circular / Centripetal)
Initial velocity and acceleration / gravity / radius parameters
Simulation Play/Pause/Reset, Step, and Speed controls
validation_cases: Constant acceleration yields linear velocity-time graph and parabolic position-time graph
Free fall under gravity g yields velocity increasing at rate g
Uniform circular motion yields constant speed with centripetal acceleration pointing inward
concepts.notes: Fully implemented with interactive canvas, acceleration vector visualization, kinematics equations, and test coverage.
